source.title: Scalable Visual Pretraining for Language Intelligence
source.authors: Yi-Ming Zhang; Zhong-Han Zhao; Wen-Wei Zhang; Hai-Teng Zhao; Tian-Yang Lin; Huan-Ze Tang; Yunhua Zhou; De-Min Song; Kui-Kun Liu; Hao-Chen Ye; Hai-An Huang; Yuzhe Gu; Hai-Jun Lv; Qi-Peng Guo; Bin Liu; Gao-Ang Wang; Kai Chen

record.tranche_reason: It varies the visual-token training budget and reports downstream benchmark outcomes, a different measure from the original loss-based scaling-law studies. It does not fit scaling laws.
record.gate_note: The study does not vary parameter count or compute, fit power laws to held-out cross-entropy, or test extrapolation from smaller runs. Its relevant results are the downstream-gain progression with VP training in Figure 2(b) and the visual-token-budget sweep in Figure 3. The other benchmark tables compare pretraining methods rather than testing scale-dependent predictability.
record.test_reason: The study compares visual with text continued pretraining on a matched corpus. 'Scalable' is used loosely. It varies neither parameters nor compute, and fits no power law to loss or downstream scores. Its 'scaling' results are a VP-to-TP gain ratio over training progress and an untuned token-budget sweep, both comparisons of its own method. Kaplan and Hoffmann appear only as background citations.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right but incomplete. The authors conclude that VP on rendered scientific PDFs outperforms text pretraining on the same corpus across four backbones, using about 20B visual tokens versus 80B text tokens. They also conclude that it improves cross-modal alignment and multimodal benchmarks without paired supervision. The 1× visual-token budget gave the best trade-off, and larger budgets may be under-tuned.
record.recipe_differences: The study varies visual-token training and evaluates downstream benchmarks; it does not measure held-out cross-entropy scaling laws, vary model size or compute, or fit extrapolative curves.
record.method_sensitivity: Downstream performance changes with visual-token budget; the authors note that the larger-budget sweep kept the learning rate and other optimization hyperparameters fixed.

fits_no_version.finding: VP's downstream gain relative to TP's grows as continued-pretraining tokens accumulate, reaching 1.27–2.88×. A larger visual-token share at fixed context is worse under the fixed learning rate.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Gains from visual-document continued pretraining over text continued pretraining grow with training tokens.

fits_no_version.finding: VP and TP reach close CPT losses (0.717 vs 0.723), yet downstream and SFT outcomes differ. The authors say pretraining loss has 'limited sensitivity' to downstream capability.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Pretraining loss compared across data representations does not predict downstream differences.

record.problems: The relevant scale evidence is limited to visual-token training and downstream gains; no power-law fit, extrapolation test, parameter-count sweep, or compute-optimal allocation is reported. The larger-budget sweep may not be fully tuned, according to the authors.

untested.parts: No shape comparison at a fixed parameter count.
Visual-document pretraining is studied, but no power-law form is fitted.
Downstream performance is not related to model scale or to pretraining loss across scales.
No fitted exponents or fitting choices are compared.

record.verdict_notes: The 'scalability' language in the paper refers to efficiency and to gains growing over training progress, not to scaling laws. The record's 'tests/T2' and its V6 labels are overreach. The rows are method-versus-baseline comparisons and should link to no version.

versions.untested_parts: No power-law fits for held-out pretraining loss against parameter count, tokens, or compute.
No predictions from small runs are compared with larger runs.
No fixed-compute comparison or compute-optimal parameter/token allocation is tested.
No controlled comparison of depth, width, or other architecture details at fixed parameter count.
Visual pretraining is studied, but the paper does not test whether the same power-law form holds for it or for other modalities and training regimes.
Tests downstream outcomes as VP training progresses and visual-token budget varies; does not test predictability across parameter count, compute, or fitted pretraining-loss relationships.
No comparison of fitted exponents, fitting choices, or curve bending away from power laws.

rows.operation_detail: Compared downstream gains as visual pretraining progressed.

conditions.value: training progress; VP uses approximately 20B visual tokens

rows.measure: Normalized VP downstream gain relative to the TP-over-base improvement
rows.note: The text says normalized gains increase steadily as training progresses; this is the reported endpoint for MMLU-Pro.
rows.check: The measure is VP gain divided by TP gain, which compares the study's own method with a baseline. It is not downstream performance as a function of scale or loss. The 1.27× is an endpoint read from Fig 2(b); the intermediate points are not read.

rows.operation_detail: Varied the visual-token budget while keeping training context fixed.

conditions.value: 1× is 8,192 tokens; larger budgets were also tested

rows.measure: Downstream benchmark performance across visual-token budgets
rows.value: The 1× setting offers the best trade-off; larger visual-token budgets have suboptimal performance.
rows.note: The paper attributes the larger-budget result partly to optimization effects and says the fixed learning rate and other hyperparameters may not be fully tuned for that sweep.
rows.check: The sweep varies the share of visual tokens within a fixed context, with the learning rate held fixed and not retuned. That is a hyperparameter choice, not model, data or compute scale. The baseline is also mislabelled: the comparison is across budgets, with TP shown only as a reference line.
